title: Horticulture Technician (Landscaping) - CZ
description_text:
Join our team at the Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo and grow your experience at one of the most unique sites in Calgary! We are seeking a permanent, full-time Horticulture Technician - Exterior to join a dynamic and dedicated Site Services Team. 

The Horticulture Technician-Exterior is responsible for the year-round care, maintenance, enhancement, and presentation of the Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo's landscapes. This role supports exceptional guest experiences through the delivery of high-quality horticultural practices, seasonal displays, landscape stewardship, irrigation management, winter operations, and collaborative support of conservation and habitat initiatives across the organization.

Our Purpose | We act for wildlife; saving species and inspiring people to join us.

Our Core Values | Drive impact, nurture connection, cultivate hope, and be bold.

What you will do:

 * Maintain the gardens, grounds and habitats at the zoo as directed by the manager; duties include weeding, planting, dead heading, digging, raking, watering, light pruning and other garden maintenance tasks.
 * Participates in landscape improvement, renovation, and capital projects including garden redesigns, planting installations, pathway improvements, and habitat beautification initiatives.
 * Operate and maintain power equipment/mobile equipment such as trimmers, blowers, tractors, and attachments.
 * Monitor plant health by identifying signs of infestation, disease, nutritional deficiencies, environmental stress, and other landscape concerns; recommend corrective action.
 * Participate in landscape improvement, renovation, and capital projects including garden redesigns, planting installations, pathway improvements, and habitat beautification initiatives.
 * Perform seasonal pruning and maintenance of ornamental trees, shrubs, and perennial collections in accordance with horticultural best practices.
 * Provides day-to-day guidance, mentorship, and task directions to seasonal staff, volunteers, and contractors to ensure work is completed safely and efficiently.
 * Responsible for maintaining sand bins, pickle mix applications, and clean-up.
 * Assist Habitats team with collection of browse material and disposal.
 * Assist with the annual ZOOLIGHTS event set-up and take-down.
 * Provides occasional support for events hosted at the Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo.
 * Collaborate with horticulture team (Botanical and Habitats) to provide snow removal and ice management.
 * Engage guests by sharing information about plants and gardens while also providing general zoo information.
 * Participate in additional training provided by the Zoo including zoonotic disease awareness, hazard assessment & control, skid steer Training, Pesticide Applicators Licensing, mobile elevated working platform, and Fall Protection.
 * Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

What you will bring: 

 * Minimum of three years of experience in landscaping, grounds maintenance, or a related field is required
 * High School Diploma or equivalent education is required
 * Valid Class 5 Driver’s License or equivalent is required
 * Landscape Gardner or Turf Maintenance Certificate is preferred
 * Demonstrated landscaping experience including grass cutting, planting, and pruning.
 * Demonstrated experience using power & non-powered hand tools
 * Flexibility to perform tasks around busy event schedule and ability to navigate changing priorities
 * Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment
 * Ability to understand, communicate, and follow instructions from both written and verbal communication

Working Conditions: 

 * This role’s regular working days include Saturday and Sunday
 * Hours of work are generally from 6:00am to 2:30pm with a flexible schedule for weekend work and occasional shift flexibility to start early or stay late
 * Working in all weather conditions, including physical work in extreme cold and hot weather
 * Walking to work sites throughout 125-acre site
 * Wear required PPE such as steel-toed boots and safety vests
 * Bending, squatting and kneeling 
 * Repetitive movements including raking, shoveling, digging, lifting and pruning.
 * Lifting, pushing and pulling up to 10-40 lbs., unassisted
 * Noise and vibrations while operating equipment
 * Exposure to fumes from operational equipment
 * Change in priorities, visitor engagement inquiries
 * Maintaining awareness of the safety of visitors, animals, contractors and coworkers
 * Movement over uneven/slippery surfaces

The Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo is an outdoor facility and all staff working at the zoo must be comfortable working in a large variety of outdoor conditions. The Wilder Institute's Calgary Zoo follows the advice of Environment Canada when responding to temperature and air quality issues.

What the Zoo Offers: 

 * Competitive compensation, vacation and flex days entitlement
 * Flexible benefits plan, including a health spending account
 * Employer matching RRSP program
 * Discounts on food, beverage, and merchandise
 * Participation in the Staff Pass Benefit plan 
 * A fun, rewarding work environment and the opportunity to work in a park full of wild animals 

Are you ready to join one of Canada’s leaders in wildlife conservation? If this position suits your skills, experience, and personal attributes, we want to talk to you. 

Apply by doing the following: 

 1. Watch this video [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8J1VH1MBXm0] about the conservation work being done at the Wilder Institute. (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8J1VH1MBXm0) 
 2. Submit your resume with a cover letter via our online application system. 
 3. Fill in the Application questions.

 Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada. 

If this position is a fit for you, we encourage you to apply with a resume and cover letter online by our application deadline: October 12, 2026.

The Wilder Institute strives to cultivate a workplace in which everyone feels welcome and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. As a conservation organization, we respect and value the diversity of all life and come together as individuals and teammates to achieve the organization’s mission and vision. We recognize the value of diversity, equity, and inclusion, and work to advance our culture to ensure diverse viewpoints are heard, and everyone has an equitable chance to succeed and thrive.

title: Animal Care Technician (On-Call in Strathmore, AB)
description_text:
Join our team at the Wilder Institute and grow your experience at one of the most unique sites in Calgary! The Wilder Institute’s Archibald Biodiversity Centre in Strathmore is seeking a fixed-term, on-call Animal Care Technician who will be responsible for completing all aspects of daily animal care and maintenance for Wilder Institutes Conservation Program animals. In addition to this, you may also assist with non dangerous animals transferred from the Calgary Zoo requiring off site temporary housing or quarantine.

Our Purpose | We act for wildlife; saving species and inspiring people to join us.

Our Core Values | Drive impact, nurture connection, cultivate hope, and be bold.

Location: Archibald Biodiversity Centre near Strathmore, Alberta

Contract:

 * Start: As soon as possible. 
 * End: March 2027
 * Schedule: 0-40 hours per week

What you will do: 

Animal Husbandry: 

 * Provide and monitor prescribed diets for a variety of animals, reporting dietary concerns or changes to management. 
 * Conduct regular assessments of animal weight, body condition, and overall health applying critical thinking to proactively identify potential health issues early. 
 * Maintain AZA standards for habitats and back-of-house areas through routine cleaning, disinfection, while actively participating in the pest management program. 
 * Identify and report any required facility and equipment maintenance. 
 * Administer prescribed treatments as needed, ensuring compliance with established protocols. 
 * Participate in animal capture and restraint procedures for veterinary procedures, shipments, and transfers under the guidance of experienced Animal Care Specialists, Supervisors, or Animal Care Technicians, ensuring all safety and welfare protocols are followed. 
 * Demonstrate and uphold established safe work practices consistently. 

Animal Welfare & Wellbeing: 

 * Observe and document the physical and psychological behavior of animals, identifying deviations from normal patterns and reporting changes to Specialists, Supervisors, or Managers in a timely manner. 
 * track behavioral training and/ or enrichment programs to promote natural species-specific behaviors and achieve specific husbandry goals. 
 * Lead and participate in various internal processes, such as behavioral enrichment and training plans, from initiation to completion, documenting outcomes comprehensively. 
 * Uphold the highest standards of animal care in accordance with our AZA accreditation, ensuring compliance with established protocols and actively contributing to risk assessments related to animal welfare under the guidance of Management.
 * Maintain accurate and detailed electronic records for Animal Health and Animal Care Teams about each animal. 
 * Update animal care records to inform and support decision making and enhance risk management practices. 
 * Identify and communicate maintenance needs for designated work areas, including, but not limited to, repairs or replacement of tools and equipment to Animal Care Specialists, Supervisors, or Managers. 
 * Troubleshoot equipment issues and train others on using equipment when necessary. 
 * Assist in educational and/or research programs as requested. 
 * Assign tasks and mentor animal care assistants tasks associated with animal welfare tasks as appropriate and as directed by Animal Care Specialists, Supervisors, and Managers. 

Related Responsibilities: 

 *  Have a diverse range of non-animal specific skills, including but not limited to vehicle operation, chemical application, plant identification, and water quality testing, to enhance operational efficiency and effectiveness.  

What you will bring: 

 * At least 2 years’ animal care experience working at a AZA accredited zoo or aquarium facility
 * Bachelors in Zoology or related field, or a combination of education and experience is required 
 * Must hold a valid Class 5 Alberta Driver’s license. 
 * Demonstrated knowledge in the care, behavior, and health of various zoological and wildlife species, with an emphasis on species-specific needs. 
 * Strong working knowledge of zoo terminology and protocols, animal welfare standards, and conservation practices. 
 * Familiarity with ZIMS (Zoological Information Management System) is highly desirable. 
 * Proven ability to adjust to frequently changing priorities and deadlines while maintaining high standards of care and attention to detail. 
 * Extensive experience working effectively in a team environment, demonstrating strong interpersonal skills and a collaborative approach, while employing effective time management and efficient strategies to achieve shared goals. 
 * Prepared to follow detailed instructions with a proactive, can-do attitude, contributing positively to team goals. 
 * Strong commitment to safety practices, ensuring a safe working environment for self and others. 
 * Ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and professionalism. 
 * Proven ability to work independently, demonstrating initiative and sound judgment in decision-making. 

Working Conditions: 

 * Comfortable working indoors and outdoors in varying weather conditions, including extreme cold, humidity, and hot climates 
 * Capable of performing physically demanding tasks unassisted, including walking, standing, crouching, climbing, reaching, pushing/pulling up to 45 kg unassisted, and lifting to 35 kg unassisted. 
 * Shift work which may be scheduled between 6:00am and 8:00pm, 7 days per week. Schedule may change at limited notice based on operational need. 
 * Call-ins may occur at any hours for emergency needs. 

The Wilder Institute's Calgary Zoo is an outdoor facility and all staff working at the zoo must be comfortable working in a large variety of outdoor conditions. The Wilder Institute's Calgary Zoo follows the advice of Environment Canada when responding to temperature and air quality issues. 

What the Zoo Offers:

 * Participation in the Staff Pass Benefit plan

 * Prop, costume and puppet maintenance including minor repairs, laundry, and storage
 * Coordination of rehearsal/performance spaces including set up/strike of outdoor performance stage and pop-up tent(s)
 * Assist in distribution of performance and preparatory materials such as schedules, scripts, rehearsal video, music files etc.

What you will bring: 

 * Completion of High School Diploma

 * Self-motivated with an ability to work independently as well as part of a collaborative team
 * Previous stage management experience is an asset
 * A love of wildlife and conversation
 * Commitment to excellent customer service to ensure visitors have a positive and memorable experience
 * A high level of curiosity, empathy and the desire to learn new skills

title: Development Officer, Partnership Fulfillment
description_text:
Join our team at the Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo and grow your experience at one of the most unique sites in Calgary! The Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo is seeking a full time Development Officer, Partnerships who will be responsible for cultivating, securing, and stewarding corporate partnerships that generate significant annual revenue in support of the Wilder Institute’s purpose and vision. 

Our Purpose | We act for wildlife; saving species and inspiring people to join us.

Our Core Values | Drive impact, nurture connection, cultivate hope, and be bold.

Location: Calgary Zoo

What you will do:        

Coordinate the Delivery of Fulfillment Obligations:

 * Coordinate with Wilder Institute’s business units to deliver on all contractually obligated partner/sponsor benefits ensuring accuracy, consistency, and timeliness. This includes but is not limited to: coordinating the design and installation of sponsor signage; coordinating the creation and posting of required social media and web content; coordinating the release of press statements; planning and coordinating engagement activities such as corporate volunteer opportunities, curated animal experiences, and conservation field observations;
 * Responsible for coordinating the removal of partnership recognition at the conclusion of partner/sponsor agreement terms;
 * Collaborate with Regional Development team members to support the delivery of all contractually obligated partner/sponsor benefits in markets across Canada, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and timeliness;
 * Support the writing and preparation of impact reports, media releases, event invitations, and other special communications in coordination with relevant team members as required;
 * Maintain internal coordination documents including cross-departmental Planners and an inventory of named assets

Maintain Strong Relationships with Corporate Partners:

 * Safeguard the confidentiality of partner/sponsor information and adhere to ethical and confidentiality guidelines;
 * Act as a key contact for partners/sponsors (in addition to the Key Relationship Manager) regarding contractual deliverables. Able to proactively resolve discrepancies in partner deliverables, with support from Key Relationship Managers and/or the Manager, Partnerships;
 * Hosting partners at coordinated engagement activities and stewardship events, acting both as a lead host and as a secondary support to the partner’s Key Relationship Manager (KRM) depending on circumstance;
 * Plan and execute partner/sponsor recognition and stewardship events. May also be required to support the coordination and delivery of Development team engagement opportunities/events;
 * Prepare, write, and deliver a quarterly partner/sponsor newsletter

Recording Partnership Fundraising and Fulfillment Activities:

 * Enter and maintain detailed records of all partner/sponsor contact, relevant history, notes, photos, and delivery of fulfillment obligations in Tessitura and company constituent records;
 * Track and report on data relevant to the Partnership Business Unit's performance and delivery of partner/sponsor benefits;
 * Coordinate with volunteers to manage bulk Tessitura entries. This includes effectively communicating the required updates to the volunteer, providing support for the data entry as required, and performing regular spot checks to ensure data is being entered correctly.

Provide Administrative Support to the Partnerships Business Unit: 

 * Support the tracking and collection of all partner/sponsor pledges and funding commitments;
 * Create an agenda, take minutes, and provide support to the Sponsorship Working Group and other internal meetings;
 * Maintain an up-to-date master sponsorship contact list;
 * Manage the partnerships email inbox, ensuring effective and timely replies

Support the Continuous Improvement of the Corporate Partner Experience:

 * Work closely with the Manager, Partnerships to advise on budgetary needs to effectively deliver partner/sponsor contractual benefits and stewardship opportunities;
 * Identify and, in collaboration with the Manager, Partnerships, lead opportunities for strategic growth within the partnership recognition program, such as developing new corporate engagement opportunities that align with existing standards.

 What you will bring:        

 * Exceptional interpersonal skills, including the ability to actively listen and build meaningful relationships with a diverse range of people;
 * Proficiency in conceptualizing and delivering high-value opportunities for external audiences. Preference given to candidates with experience delivering these opportunities to a corporate-focused audience;
 * Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office products, including Outlook, Word, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint;
 * Ability to take initiative and work independently in service of established team goals;
 * Excellent time and project management skills with a proven ability to meet competing deadlines in an organized manner. Includes the ability to demonstrate a high degree of flexibility to rapidly changing scenarios;
 * Ability to maintain confidentiality and operate in accordance with the Donor Bill of Rights.

Working Conditions:       

 * Ability to work some evenings and weekends required. This may include attending networking events, supporting Wilder Institute event delivery, or other similar fundraising-related activities. 
 * This role sits at a desk or other meeting space for approximately 90% of the time, with the opportunity to integrate more movement as appropriate for certain meetings. The remaining time involves moving across various terrain to support the set up and execution of events and partner hosting opportunities. 
 * May be asked to work outdoors in various weather conditions in support of Development events and other partner hosting needs. 
 * Occasional requirement to move objects up to 20kgs. 
 * This is a hybrid role with the ability to work from home. Role is expected to be flexible with work from home schedule to accommodate partner meetings, hosting requirements, and other meetings and events that cannot be pivoted to a virtual format. 
 * Ability to commute to participate in in-person meetings and events at locations other than the Wilder Institute headquarters. 
 * Office environment is open concept with personal cubicles for each team member; there is some natural noise from working in the shared environment. 
 * Position will occasionally need to interact with animals in close proximity and may be required to wear a mask and gloves, use a foot bath, or use other PPE as required to safely engage in this activity. 

The Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo is an outdoor facility and all staff working at the zoo must be comfortable working in a large variety of outdoor conditions. The Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo follows the advice of Environment Canada when responding to temperature and air quality issues.

What the Zoo Offers: 

 * Competitive compensation, vacation and flex days entitlement
 * Flexible benefits plan, including a health spending account
 * Employer matching RRSP program
 * Discounts on food, beverage, and merchandise
 * Participation in the Staff Pass Benefit plan

title: Building Technician
description_text:
Join our team at the Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo and grow your experience at one of the most unique sites in Calgary! The Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo is seeking a full time Building Technician who will be responsible for the safe and efficient operation and maintenance of all HVAC systems & other mechanical systems in the Calgary Zoo.

Our Purpose | We act for wildlife; saving species and inspiring people to join us.

Our Core Values | Drive impact, nurture connection, cultivate hope, and be bold.

Location: Calgary Zoo

What you will do:

 * Ensures buildings, structures, and facilities are fully functional and operating safely and efficiently.
 * Carries out daily building maintenance tasks in a timely, efficient and safe manner.
 * Maintains and troubleshoots mechanical and control systems as required.
 * Works with the Zoo’s building automation and control systems – Metasys and RCK Controls.
 * Monitors and maintains animal life support systems.
 * Provides regular servicing of the Zoo’s commercial kitchen equipment.
 * Performs preventive maintenance tasks as per schedule.
 * Maintains daily ABSA logs, including activities, changes and on-going events.
 * Provides on-call service in accordance with policies and procedures in order to ensure 24/7 operation of all critical systems.
 * Schedules work with contractors as required to maintain mechanical systems.
 * Purchases materials as required from suppliers as per zoo's procurement policy.
 * Executes work orders as assigned.
 * Is a team player. Interacts with trades and other staff Zoo wide to ensure a collaborative team environment.
 * Additional training that may be required and provided by the Zoo includes; WHMIS, workforce orientation, vehicle operator training, zoonotic disease awareness, skid steer training, respiratory protection, pest control, ozone awareness training, lock out/tag out, hazard assessment & control, forklift training, fire extinguisher training, fall protection, confined space, Code Adam, boom lift training, asbestos/mold training and transportation of dangerous goods.

What you will bring: 

 * Minimum of 5 years Building Operations experience.
 * Experience with Building Management softwares and Preventive Maintenance systems required.
 * Proven ability to troubleshoot systems.
 * Proven experience with heating plants, HVAC, water filtration, electricity, pneumatics, hydraulics, controls, chillers, ozone generation, hydronics and fire alarm systems.
 * Experience maintaining commercial kitchen equipment is an asset.
 * Well-developed organizational and communication skills and ability to work with other trades required.
 * Self-motivated and able to work independently required.
 * Customer service focus required.

Working Conditions: 

 * This position requires the individual to work under various conditions: adverse weather conditions, various heights, physical demands (heavy lifting, walking, etc.), confined spaces, pungent odors, near animals, and near zoo visitors.
 * 8-hour shifts, weekends and a weekly “On-Call” rotational schedule are part of the normal work schedule, day shifts only.
 * Overtime as required.
 * Required to lift items weighing over 20 kilograms.

title: Event Host
description_text:
Join our team at the Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo and grow your experience at one of the most unique sites in Calgary! The Wilder Institute’s Calgary Zoo is seeking seasonal Event Hosts to help deliver exceptional guest experiences, especially during our upcoming ZOOLIGHTS. 

Event Hosts create a welcoming and engaging environment for visitors of all ages by providing outstanding customer service, facilitating event activities and experiences, and by supporting the safe and efficient operation of ZOOLIGHTS and other events as needed.

Our Purpose | We act for wildlife; saving species and inspiring people to join us.

Our Core Values | Drive impact, nurture connection, cultivate hope, and be bold.

Contract:

 * Start Date: late October to early November
 * End Date: January 3, 2027

Important dates to note:

 * New employee orientation will take place on October 31 or November 2, 2026 from 9:00am to 12:30pm.
 * Mandatory ZOOLIGHTS training will take place on November 4 and 5, 2026, during evening hours (anticipated approximately 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.).

What you will do:

 * Facilitate engaging and memorable event experiences that are welcoming, inclusive, and visitor-focused.
 * Provide exceptional customer service by answering questions, assisting with problem-solving, and responding to visitor concerns in a calm and professional manner.
 * Initiate conversations and deliver organizational messaging in a manner that reflects the zoo’s brand, voice, and commitment to wildlife conservation.
 * Share information about zoo animals, amenities, ZOOLIGHTS experiences, and conservation efforts, as appropriate.
 * Support the safe and efficient movement of visitors throughout events, including wayfinding, queuing, crowd flow, and reinforcing event rules and guidelines.
 * Facilitate event activities and experiences, including speaking to groups with or without amplification.
 * Set up, maintain, and take down event spaces and equipment as required.
 * Work collaboratively with zoo staff, volunteers, contractors, and external partners to support the successful delivery of events.
 * Provide in-the-moment guidance, logistical support, and mentorship to zoo volunteers to assist them in completing their assigned responsibilities.
 * Respond to changing event needs and assist other teams with operational requirements as needed.

What you will bring: 

 * High school diploma or equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant experience is required. Post-secondary education in these fields is an asset.
 * Minimum 1 year of experience in customer service, hospitality, tourism, education, recreation, events, or another public-facing environment is required
 * Strong verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide respectful, inclusive, and professional customer service to a diverse range of visitors. 
 * Demonstrated ability to remain calm and professional when responding to customer concerns, challenging situations, or conflict. 
 * Ability to effectively work independently and collaboratively with staff, volunteers, contractors, and partners. 
 * Deliver organizational messaging in a manner consistent with the zoo's brand, voice, and conservation goals. 
 * Ability to work in a dynamic event environment and respond appropriately to changing circumstances. 
 * Basic computer skills and ability to use common workplace communication tools, including email and Microsoft OneNote. 

Working Conditions: 

 * Exposure to outdoor conditions as work is performed primarily outdoors throughout the event spaces, including during winter conditions such as cold temperatures, wind, snow, and precipitation.
 * Move throughout the zoo grounds and remain on duty in a variety of event locations featuring uneven surfaces/terrain, crowds, and event-related equipment.
 * Regularly stand, move, and interact with visitors for extended periods throughout the shift.
 * Regularly move event materials, supplies, and equipment, including pushing and pulling wagons and carts.
 * May occasionally move supplies or equipment requiring additional physical effort, with assistance or appropriate equipment as needed. 
 * Shift times vary and will include evenings, weekends, holidays, and other scheduled event dates.
